name: Spanish Squat
description: The Spanish squat uses a resistance band looped around a fixed post at knee height, which the lifter presses the shins against during the squat. This creates a vertical shin angle by preventing the knees from traveling forward, shifting nearly all load to the quadriceps while decompressing the patellar tendon. It is widely used in rehabilitation settings for patellar tendinopathy and knee pain.

execution.starting_position: Loop a heavy resistance band around a fixed post at approximately knee height. Step into the band with both shins pressing against it. Stand with feet hip-width apart, shins vertical against the band.
execution.setup_instructions: Secure a resistance band to a stable vertical post. The band should contact the front of the shins at mid-shin level when you are in your squat position.
steps: Step 1: Press the shins into the band and brace your core.
Step 2: Keeping the shins vertical and pressing against the band, squat straight down.
Step 3: Descend to depth while maintaining an upright torso — the band prevents knees from traveling forward.
Step 4: Drive through the heels to return to standing while maintaining shin contact with the band.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale at the top, exhale on the ascent.
common_mistakes: Allowing the knees to drift forward past the band, losing the therapeutic effect
Leaning too far back, shifting load away from the quads
safety_considerations: This exercise is used therapeutically — progress load conservatively if treating patellar tendinopathy
Consult a physiotherapist if using for knee rehabilitation
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Descend as deep as comfortable while maintaining vertical shins and upright torso.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 3-2-1-0 (slow descent with pause) for rehabilitation use. Faster for strength.
